---

Rust SDK for the [ACT protocol](https://github.com/actcore/act-spec) — define tools as plain functions, compile to `.wasm`, serve over MCP or HTTP.

## Quick start

```rust
use act_sdk::prelude::*;

#[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
struct GreetArgs {
    name: String,
}

#[act_component(name = "greeter", version = "0.1.0", description = "A greeter")]
mod component {
    use super::*;

    #[act_tool(description = "Say hello", read_only)]
    fn greet(args: GreetArgs) -> ActResult<String> {
        Ok(format!("Hello, {}!", args.name))
    }
}
```

```sh
cargo build --target wasm32-wasip2 --release
act serve target/wasm32-wasip2/release/greeter.wasm
# or
act mcp target/wasm32-wasip2/release/greeter.wasm
```

## Workspace crates

| Crate | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [`act-sdk`](act-sdk/) | SDK with `#[act_component]` and `#[act_tool]` macros |
| [`act-sdk-macros`](act-sdk-macros/) | Proc macro implementation |
| [`act-types`](act-types/) | Shared types, CBOR utilities, JSON-RPC and MCP wire formats |

## Features

- **`#[act_tool]`** — derive tool metadata, JSON Schema, and CBOR serialization from a plain Rust function
- **Streaming** — mark tools with `streaming` and use `ActContext` to emit progress events
- **Typed config** — define a config struct, get automatic JSON Schema generation and validation
- **MCP + HTTP** — same `.wasm` works with both transports, zero code changes

## Examples

| Example | What it shows |
|---------|---------------|
| [`hello-sdk`](examples/hello-sdk/) | Basic tools, streaming with `ctx.send_progress()` |
| [`config-sdk`](examples/config-sdk/) | Typed component configuration |
| [`http-client-sdk`](examples/http-client-sdk/) | Outbound HTTP via WASI |
| [`hello-world`](examples/hello-world/) | Minimal component without SDK (raw wit-bindgen) |
| [`http-client`](examples/http-client/) | Raw HTTP client without SDK |
| [`counter`](examples/counter/) | Stateful counter |

## Building

Requires Rust nightly (for `wasm32-wasip2` async support):

```sh
# Build all examples
cargo build --target wasm32-wasip2 --release

# Run tests (host-side, not wasm)
cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

See [`rust-toolchain.toml`](rust-toolchain.toml) for the pinned toolchain.

# ACT SDK v0.2.0 Spec Update Implementation Plan

Source: https://github.com/actcore/act-sdk-rs/blob/main/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-15-v0.2.0-spec-update.md

# ACT SDK v0.2.0 Spec Update Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (if subagents available) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Update act-sdk-rs to match the ACT v0.2.0 spec: remove `config` parameter, remove `get-info`/`get-config-schema`, add `get-metadata-schema`, pass metadata via `tool-call.metadata`.

**Architecture:** The WIT submodule (`wit/deps/act-core`) already has v0.2.0 WIT. We update the world.wit files to reference `@0.2.0`, update the proc macro to generate the new trait impl, update act-types to replace `Config` with metadata patterns, and update examples.

**Tech Stack:** Rust, wit-bindgen, proc_macro2/syn/quote, schemars, serde, ciborium

---

## Task 1: Update WIT world files to v0.2.0

**Files:**
- Modify: `examples/hello-sdk/wit/world.wit`
- Modify: `examples/config-sdk/wit/world.wit`
- Modify: `examples/http-client-sdk/wit/world.wit`
- Modify: `examples/hello-world/wit/world.wit`
- Modify: `examples/counter/wit/world.wit`
- Modify: `examples/http-client/wit/world.wit`

- [ ] **Step 1: Update all world.wit files**

Change `@0.1.6` to `@0.2.0` in every `world.wit`:

```wit
package component:impl;

world component-world {
  export act:core/tool-provider@0.2.0;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Update WIT submodule pointer**

The submodule `wit/deps/act-core` must point to the commit with v0.2.0 WIT:

```bash
cd wit/deps/act-core
git pull origin main
cd ../../..
git add wit/deps/act-core
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify WIT parsing**

```bash
cargo check --target wasm32-wasip2 -p hello-sdk 2>&1 | head -20
```

Expected: may fail on trait mismatch (no `get_info`, `get_config_schema`) — that's expected, confirms WIT is parsed.

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit**

```bash
git add examples/*/wit/world.wit wit/deps/act-core
git commit -m "feat: update WIT to act:core@0.2.0"
```

---

## Task 2: Update proc macro — remove `get-info` and `get-config-schema`

**Files:**
- Modify: `act-sdk-macros/src/component.rs`

The v0.2.0 `tool-provider` trait no longer has `get_info()` or `get_config_schema()`. It has `get_metadata_schema(metadata)` instead. `call-tool` no longer takes `config`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Update the generated trait impl in `component.rs`**

Replace the `impl exports::act::core::tool_provider::Guest` block. Remove `get_info()` and `get_config_schema()`. Add `get_metadata_schema()`. Change `list_tools` signature. Change `call_tool` signature.

In `component.rs`, replace the generated output (inside `generate()`) from line ~103:

```rust
    let output = quote! {
        // WIT bindings generation
        wit_bindgen::generate!({
            path: "wit",
            world: "component-world",
            generate_all,
        });

        // User-defined items from the module body
        #(#user_items)*

        // Generated hidden arg structs
        #(#arg_structs)*

        /// Convert a RawStreamEvent to a WIT StreamEvent.
        fn __raw_to_wit(raw: ::act_sdk::context::RawStreamEvent) -> act::core::types::StreamEvent {
            match raw {
                ::act_sdk::context::RawStreamEvent::Content { data, mime_type, metadata } => {
                    act::core::types::StreamEvent::Content(act::core::types::ContentPart {
                        data,
                        mime_type,
                        metadata,
                    })
                }
                ::act_sdk::context::RawStreamEvent::Error { kind, message, default_language: _ } => {
                    act::core::types::StreamEvent::Error(act::core::types::ToolError {
                        kind,
                        message: act::core::types::LocalizedString::Plain(message),
                        metadata: vec![],
                    })
                }
            }
        }

        struct __ActComponent;

        export!(__ActComponent);

        impl exports::act::core::tool_provider::Guest for __ActComponent {
            async fn get_metadata_schema(
                _metadata: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>,
            ) -> Option<String> {
                #config_schema_expr
            }

            async fn list_tools(
                _metadata: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>,
            ) -> Result<act::core::types::ListToolsResponse, act::core::types::ToolError> {
                Ok(act::core::types::ListToolsResponse {
                    metadata: vec![],
                    tools: vec![
                        #(#tool_defs),*
                    ],
                })
            }

            async fn call_tool(
                call: act::core::types::ToolCall,
            ) -> wit_bindgen::rt::async_support::StreamReader<act::core::types::StreamEvent> {
                let (mut writer, reader) = wit_stream::new::<act::core::types::StreamEvent>();

                wit_bindgen::spawn(async move {
                    let __default_lang = #default_lang;
                    match call.name.as_str() {
                        #(#call_arms)*
                        __other => {
                            let _ = writer.write_all(vec![
                                act::core::types::StreamEvent::Error(act::core::types::ToolError {
                                    kind: ::act_sdk::constants::ERR_NOT_FOUND.to_string(),
                                    message: act::core::types::LocalizedString::Plain(format!("Tool '{}' not found", __other)),
                                    metadata: vec![],
                                })
                            ]).await;
                        }
                    }
                });

                reader
            }
        }
    };
```

Key changes:
- Removed `fn get_info()`
- Removed `fn get_config_schema()`
- Added `async fn get_metadata_schema(_metadata: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>) -> Option<String>`
- `list_tools` takes `_metadata: Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>` instead of `_config: Option<Vec<u8>>`
- `call_tool` takes only `call: act::core::types::ToolCall` (no config)

- [ ] **Step 2: Update config_schema_expr generation**

The `config_schema_expr` currently generates a schema from the config type. Rename the variable to `metadata_schema_expr` for clarity. The logic stays the same — it generates a JSON Schema from the config type if one exists.

In `generate()`, rename:
```rust
    let metadata_schema_expr =
        if let Some(config_type) = tools.iter().find_map(|t| t.config_type.as_ref()) {
            quote! {
                Some(::act_sdk::__private::serde_json::to_string(
                    &::act_sdk::__private::schemars::schema_for!(#config_type)
                ).unwrap_or_else(|_| r#"{"type":"object"}"#.to_string()))
            }
        } else {
            quote! { None }
        };
```

And use `#metadata_schema_expr` in `get_metadata_schema`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Update `gen_call_arm` — remove config handling**

In `gen_call_arm`, the `ctx_setup` block currently deserializes `_config`. Since config is now in metadata, and the SDK config pattern needs rethinking (see Task 3), for now change the context setup to extract config from `call.metadata`:

Replace the `ctx_setup` block for config_type case:
```rust
    let ctx_setup = if tool.has_context {
        if let Some(config_type) = &tool.config_type {
            quote! {
                let __config: #config_type = {
                    // Extract config from well-known metadata keys
                    let __metadata_map: ::act_sdk::__private::serde_json::Value = {
                        let mut map = ::act_sdk::__private::serde_json::Map::new();
                        for (k, v) in &call.metadata {
                            if let Ok(val) = ::act_sdk::cbor::from_cbor::<::act_sdk::__private::serde_json::Value>(v) {
                                map.insert(k.clone(), val);
                            }
                        }
                        ::act_sdk::__private::serde_json::Value::Object(map)
                    };
                    match ::act_sdk::__private::serde_json::from_value(__metadata_map) {
                        Ok(v) => v,
                        Err(e) => {
                            let _ = writer.write_all(vec![
                                act::core::types::StreamEvent::Error(act::core::types::ToolError {
                                    kind: ::act_sdk::constants::ERR_INVALID_ARGS.to_string(),
                                    message: act::core::types::LocalizedString::Plain(format!("Failed to deserialize metadata: {}", e)),
                                    metadata: vec![],
                                })
                            ]).await;
                            return;
                        }
                    }
                };
                let mut __ctx = ::act_sdk::ActContext::__new(__config, __default_lang.to_string());
            }
        } else {
            quote! {
                let mut __ctx = ::act_sdk::ActContext::__new((), __default_lang.to_string());
            }
        }
    } else {
        quote! {}
    };
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run macro tests**

```bash
cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p act-sdk-macros
```

Expected: PASS (macro tests are unit-level, may not exercise WIT bindings)

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add act-sdk-macros/src/component.rs
git commit -m "feat: update proc macro for act:core@0.2.0 — remove get-info, add get-metadata-schema"
```

## Task 3: Update act-types — replace Config with metadata helpers

**Files:**
- Modify: `act-types/src/types.rs`
- Modify: `act-types/src/http.rs`
- Modify: `act-types/src/lib.rs`

- [ ] **Step 1: Remove `Config` type, update re-exports**

In `act-types/src/types.rs`, remove the `Config` newtype (it wrapped `Vec<u8>` for config CBOR). The concept is replaced by `Metadata` which already exists.

In `act-types/src/lib.rs`, remove `Config` from the re-export:
```rust
pub use types::{ActError, ActResult, Args, LocalizedString, Metadata};
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Update HTTP types — config → metadata**

In `act-types/src/http.rs`:
- Rename `ConfigRequest.config` to `metadata`
- Rename `ToolCallRequest.config` to `metadata`
- Update `ServerInfo` — remove `config_schema` if present
- Add `metadata_schema` endpoint types if needed

```rust
pub struct MetadataSchemaRequest {
    pub metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

pub struct ConfigRequest {  // rename to MetadataRequest
    pub metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

pub struct ToolCallRequest {
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub arguments: serde_json::Value,
    pub metadata: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Remove Config tests, update Metadata tests**

Remove `config_from_json_opt_*` tests. Ensure `Metadata` tests cover the same patterns.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run act-types tests**

```bash
cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p act-types
```

Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add act-types/
git commit -m "feat(act-types): replace Config with metadata patterns for v0.2.0"
```

## Task 5: Update act-cli host bindings

**Note:** act-cli is a separate repo. This task documents what needs to change but may be executed separately.

**Files:**
- Modify: `../act-cli/src/runtime.rs` — update bindings for new WIT
- Modify: `../act-cli/src/main.rs` — remove config parameter passing
- Modify: `../act-cli/src/http.rs` — config → metadata in HTTP handlers
- Modify: `../act-cli/src/mcp.rs` — config → metadata in MCP handlers

Key changes:
- `get_info()` → read `act:component` custom section from WASM binary
- `get_config_schema()` → `get_metadata_schema(metadata)`
- `list_tools(config)` → `list_tools(metadata)`
- `call_tool(config, call)` → `call_tool(call)` with metadata in `tool-call.metadata`
- CLI `--config` flag → `--metadata` or parsed into metadata key-value pairs

# Security Policy

Source: https://github.com/actcore/act-sdk-rs/blob/main/SECURITY.md

# Security Policy

Security is a core priority of the ACT project, not an afterthought.

## Reporting Vulnerabilities

If you discover a security vulnerability, please report it privately via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/actcore/act-spec/security/advisories/new) or email security@actcore.dev.

Do **not** open a public issue for security vulnerabilities.

## Supply Chain Security

- **Trusted publishing.** All ACT packages use OpenID Connect (OIDC) trusted publishing for crates.io, PyPI, and npm. No long-lived API tokens are stored in CI. We encourage component authors to adopt the same practice.
- **Build provenance.** Every release includes Sigstore-based build provenance attestation, verifiable via `gh attestation verify`.
- **SBOM.** Every release ships a CycloneDX SBOM so users can audit the full dependency tree.

## Sandbox Model

Components run in WebAssembly's capability-based sandbox. No filesystem, network, or system access is available unless explicitly granted by the operator via `--allow-dir` or `--allow-fs` flags. This is enforced by the Wasmtime runtime, not by the component.
